rows.date_note: Ming reign era used in Joseon dating; the year number gives the exact year.
rows.what_it_tells: A dated buncheong — a fixed point for the style of undated items.
rows.cautions: A date on a tomb tablet fixes that tablet; it dates other items only by comparison.

facts.text: Dated items: epitaphs of 成化七年 (1471) and 成化八年 (1472) at NMK; a brushed-slip jar of 成化十四年 (1478); an iron-painted epitaph of 成化二十三年 (1487) from the 1927 Gyeryongsan kiln excavation, also photographed on an NMK glass plate.

rows.meaning: Hongzhi reign era (1488–1505)
rows.technique: inlaid or iron-painted on epitaph tablets; inlaid on vessels
rows.where_on_object: face of the epitaph tablet or interior of the vessel
rows.date_note: Ming reign era used in Joseon dating; the year number gives the exact year.
rows.what_it_tells: A dated buncheong — a fixed point for the style of undated items.
rows.cautions: A date on a tomb tablet fixes that tablet; it dates other items only by comparison.

facts.text: An iron-painted epitaph sherd of 弘治三年 (1490) from the Gyeryongsan kilns; NMK glass plates record it.

rows.meaning: Jiajing reign era (1522–1566)
rows.technique: inlaid or iron-painted on epitaph tablets; inlaid on vessels
rows.where_on_object: face of the epitaph tablet or interior of the vessel
rows.date_note: Ming reign era used in Joseon dating; the year number gives the exact year.
rows.what_it_tells: A dated buncheong — a fixed point for the style of undated items.
rows.cautions: Shows buncheong still made for epitaphs in the 16th century, well after office marks stop.

facts.text: An iron-painted epitaph sherd of 嘉靖十五年 (1536) from the Gyeryongsan kilns (NMK glass plate); a 嘉靖十九年 (1540) epitaph at NMK.

rows.meaning: 'Heaven', first character of the Thousand Character Classic (千字文) sequence 天地玄黃
rows.technique: incised through the glaze (線刻/음각), inside the foot; sometimes stippled marks added later
rows.date_note: From the founding of the Gwangju official kiln (c.1467) to the 1560s switch to 左·右 (kgh2013, kkj2012); found with 天 at 무갑리 14호, dated by a 1548 epitaph (kkj2012).
rows.what_it_tells: Fine royal-use ware from the Saongwon official kiln at Gwangju, late 15th to mid 16th century. One of four (five with 宇) parallel marks.
rows.cautions: Meaning disputed (see facts). The mark is incised before firing, so it is a kiln mark, but it does not by itself date an item within c.1467-1560s. Stippled hangul names on 天-marked sherds were added later at the place of use.

facts.text: 天, 地, 玄, 黃 are incised one character per vessel into the glaze inside the foot of fine bowls and dishes found at the 15th-century Gwangju kiln sites of 우산리, 번천리 and 도마리.
facts.quote: 황(黃)의 글자를 각각 한 자씩 선각

facts.text: 天 and 玄 sherds were found at 무갑리 kiln 14, which a 嘉靖二十七年 (1548) porcelain epitaph dates to around 1548; 地 and 天 sherds occur at 학동리 kilns 14 and 15.
The Thousand Character Classic marks were used from the founding of the Gwangju official kiln (c.1467) until the 1560s, when 左·右 replaced them.
Park Jungmin dates 天地玄黃-incised wares to the second half of the 15th and first half of the 16th century.

Scholars disagree on what 天·地·玄·黃 mean: names of the palace storehouses 天字庫, 地字庫 … at Gyeongbokgung (Encykorea; 윤용이), supervision marks made by officials before firing (윤용이), categories of use fixed in advance (박정민 2012), the four 提調 directors of the Saongwon (박정민, seen only in a search excerpt), or a control system for production, stock and issue (김귀한 2013).
facts.quote: ‘天字庫’·‘地字庫’ 등이 있어 그 所用의 구분 기호

facts.text: 天 is found on palace-site sherds together with stippled hangul names, e.g. 큰 (king's kitchen), 동쇼 (crown prince's kitchen), 혜슌 (Princess Hyesun, before 1522) and 졔긔 (ritual vessel).
facts.quote: 天 incised on White Porcelain Dish

rows.meaning: 'Earth', second character of the 天地玄黃 sequence
rows.technique: incised through the glaze inside the foot; at palace sites also stippled (정각) beside a 左 mark
rows.date_note: As for 天; 地 still occurs with 左·右 at 관음리 10호 (1559 to late 1560s), the transition kiln (kkj2012).
rows.what_it_tells: Fine Gwangju official-kiln ware of c.1467-1560s for palace or office use.
rows.cautions: Meaning disputed (see 天). A 地 stippled beside an incised 左 on a Gyeongbokgung sherd shows the two systems overlapped briefly.

facts.text: 地 is incised inside the foot of official-kiln wares from 우산리 (catalogued sherd 기증1-119) and other 15th-16th-century Gwangju kilns.
At 관음리 kiln 10 (1559 to late 1560s) 地 occurs together with 左 and 右, so the switch from 天地玄黃 to 左右 happened there.
facts.quote: ‘左’·‘右’銘 뿐만 아니라 ‘地’銘이 음각된 백자편

facts.text: A sherd from the 함화당 site in Gyeongbokgung has 左 incised and 地 stippled (정각) beside it, so the two systems coexisted for a time.
facts.quote: ‘左’銘이 음각된 곳 옆에 정으로 쪼아 ‘地’銘

facts.text: The Thousand Character Classic marks were used from the founding of the Gwangju official kiln (c.1467) until the 1560s, when 左·右 replaced them.

Scholars disagree on what 天·地·玄·黃 mean: names of the palace storehouses 天字庫, 地字庫 … at Gyeongbokgung (Encykorea; 윤용이), supervision marks made by officials before firing (윤용이), categories of use fixed in advance (박정민 2012), the four 提調 directors of the Saongwon (박정민, seen only in a search excerpt), or a control system for production, stock and issue (김귀한 2013).
facts.quote: ‘天字庫’·‘地字庫’ 등이 있어 그 所用의 구분 기호

rows.meaning: 'Dark', third character of the 天地玄黃 sequence
rows.technique: incised through the glaze inside the foot
rows.date_note: As for 天; 玄 sherds come from 번천리 7·8호 (c.1552-1558) and 무갑리 14호 (c.1548) (kkj2012).
rows.what_it_tells: Fine Gwangju official-kiln ware of c.1467-1560s.
rows.cautions: Meaning disputed (see 天).

facts.text: 玄 and 地 sherds come from 번천리 kilns 7 and 8, part of the 번천리 group dated 1552-1558 by porcelain epitaphs.
Two Gyeongbokgung sherds incised 玄 carry the stippled name 영양 (Prince Yeongyang, married c.1532), i.e. fine palace ware used before c.1532.
facts.quote: 玄 incised on White Porcelain Shard

facts.text: The Thousand Character Classic marks were used from the founding of the Gwangju official kiln (c.1467) until the 1560s, when 左·右 replaced them.

Scholars disagree on what 天·地·玄·黃 mean: names of the palace storehouses 天字庫, 地字庫 … at Gyeongbokgung (Encykorea; 윤용이), supervision marks made by officials before firing (윤용이), categories of use fixed in advance (박정민 2012), the four 提調 directors of the Saongwon (박정민, seen only in a search excerpt), or a control system for production, stock and issue (김귀한 2013).
facts.quote: ‘天字庫’·‘地字庫’ 등이 있어 그 所用의 구분 기호

rows.meaning: 'Yellow', fourth character of the 天地玄黃 sequence
rows.technique: incised through the glaze inside the foot
rows.date_note: As for 天; 黃 sherds are recorded at 열미리 5호 (kkj2012).
rows.what_it_tells: Fine Gwangju official-kiln ware of c.1467-1560s.
rows.cautions: Meaning disputed (see 天).

facts.text: 黃 sherds are recorded at 열미리 kiln 5, one of the early-16th-century official kiln sites.
黃-incised palace sherds carry stippled hangul 웃궁 (queen dowager's private store) or 큰쇼 (king's kitchen), added at the place of use.
facts.quote: 黃 incised and ilgong (一공) stippled

facts.text: The Thousand Character Classic marks were used from the founding of the Gwangju official kiln (c.1467) until the 1560s, when 左·右 replaced them.

Scholars disagree on what 天·地·玄·黃 mean: names of the palace storehouses 天字庫, 地字庫 … at Gyeongbokgung (Encykorea; 윤용이), supervision marks made by officials before firing (윤용이), categories of use fixed in advance (박정민 2012), the four 提調 directors of the Saongwon (박정민, seen only in a search excerpt), or a control system for production, stock and issue (김귀한 2013).
facts.quote: ‘天字庫’·‘地字庫’ 등이 있어 그 所用의 구분 기호

rows.meaning: 'Universe', fifth character of the Thousand Character Classic (天地玄黃宇宙洪荒)
rows.technique: incised through the glaze inside the foot
rows.date_note: Assumed contemporary with 天地玄黃 because of the same technique and ware quality; not yet found at a kiln site (kkj2012).
rows.what_it_tells: Fine official-kiln ware of the 天地玄黃 period; very rare.
rows.cautions: Known only from Seoul consumption sites (어영청지, 종묘광장, 청진동); meaning not settled. Do not confuse with 右 (also read u).

facts.text: Sherds incised 宇 inside the foot were found at the 어영청 site, around 종묘광장 and at 청진동 in Seoul, but none yet at a kiln site.
facts.quote: ‘宇’銘이 음각된 백자가 어영청지(御營廳址)와

facts.text: Park Jungmin explains the rarity of 宇 as small production: extra demand was given a new character mark, otherwise stippled marks were added.
facts.quote: ‘宇’명이 다른 字號들에 비해 출토량이 극히 적은

rows.meaning: 'Left': the left production team (左班) of the official kiln
rows.technique: incised through the glaze inside the foot; from 1606 followed by a sexagenary year, from 1626-27 also by numbers (month and day)
rows.date_note: 1560s to 1690s (kgh2013); 左·右 sherds also at 관음리 17·18호 into the early 18th century (kgh2022; kkj2022).
rows.what_it_tells: Regular annual-tribute ware (연례진상) of the Gwangju official kiln, made by one of two production teams; with a 干支 it gives a year of production.
rows.cautions: 左 alone does not date an item closely (c.1560-1716). With a ganji the 60-year cycle must be resolved by kiln context, foot shape and firing supports.

facts.text: 左·右 replaced 天地玄黃 in the 1560s; from 1606 a sexagenary year was added and from 1626-27 numbers; the marks stop around the 1690s.
左 and 右 name the kiln's production teams (분반), an interpretation first proposed by 정양모 (1986) as 'production groups'.
From the 1560s official-kiln ware was split into annual-tribute ware marked 左·右 and extra ware (別器) marked 別.
左·右 sherds were also collected at 관음리 kilns 17 and 18, so the marks continued into the early 18th century.
The Saongwon's branch kiln moved about every ten years to find firewood, so each run of ganji belongs to one village site.
facts.quote: 將迫十年, 樹木已盡

rows.meaning: 'Right': the right production team (右班) of the official kiln
rows.technique: incised through the glaze inside the foot, often with a sexagenary year and numbers
rows.date_note: As for 左.
rows.what_it_tells: As for 左: annual-tribute ware of the Gwangju official kiln, c.1560s-early 18th century.
rows.cautions: As for 左. Do not confuse with 宇 (also read u).

facts.text: 右 is the counterpart of 左 and follows the same chronology (1560s-1690s, with ganji from 1606).
別右庚 on a 선동리 dish means extra ware made by the right team (右班) in the 庚辰 year, 1640.

rows.meaning: 'Extra': ware fired outside the regular quota (別燔) for the royal family or court (別器)
rows.technique: incised through the glaze inside the foot, often with a ganji; one hangul 별 incised on a jar lid
rows.date_note: 1560s-1640s (kgh2022); a hangul 별 lid from 번천리 9호 (1550s) may push the start earlier; the latest is 別右庚 (1640) and plain 別 at 선동리 1호 (1640-48).
rows.what_it_tells: Special-order official-kiln ware of the late 16th to mid 17th century, often of better quality than 左·右 ware.
rows.cautions: The meaning of 別 alone (state or royal use) cannot be pinned down; extra ware was also re-assigned. 別 at consumption sites cannot always be dated.

facts.text: 別-marked white porcelain was made at the official kiln from the 1560s to the 1640s, forming a dual system with 左·右.
Extra firings (別燔) put pressure on the official kiln after the 1501 tribute reform, which Kim Kwihan links to the appearance of 別-marked ware in the 1560s.
別 occurs with 左·右 at 곤지암리 1호 (c.1572), with ganji at 왕산리 (別丁卯 1627) and 상림리 (別辛未 1631, 別壬申 1632, 別丙子 1636), and 別右庚 at 선동리 (1640).
A jar lid from 번천리 kiln 9 (1550s, Ewha Womans University Museum) has 별 written in hangul.
From about 1659 annual ware and extra ware used different white clays (원주·서산 vs 경주·선천), so the 別 mark was no longer needed and disappeared.

rows.meaning: Prefix before 左/右; read by Kim Kyoung-joong as the official in charge (관리책임자)
rows.technique: incised inside the foot; once painted in iron on a saggar-lid plate
rows.date_note: 元庚辰/元庚右 at 선동리 (1640); 元右 at 궁평리 2호 (1690s) and 관음리 17호 (to 1716) (kkj2022).
rows.what_it_tells: A late-17th to early-18th-century official-kiln mark; 元右(左) without ganji points to 궁평리/관음리 (c.1690s-1716).
rows.cautions: Single scholar's reading of the meaning.

facts.text: 元 before 右 marks the official in charge; apart from 궁평리 2호 (己七元右) it is not found at earlier kilns, and 관음리 17호 yields 元右(左)□□.
선동리 kiln 2 yields 右+元庚 and 左+元庚辰 (1640), kiln 1 元庚右.

rows.meaning: Unexplained mark of the early-18th-century 관음리 kilns
rows.technique: incised inside the foot
rows.date_note: 관음리 17호 (c.1703/1709-1716) and 18·19·35호 (1721-1733) per kkj2022; also from the 군기시 site in Seoul.
rows.what_it_tells: Points to the 관음리 official kilns of the early 18th century.
rows.cautions: Meaning unknown; reading of the hangul-like hanja uncertain (another reading '二山' was corrected to 另工).

facts.text: NMK survey sherds from 관음리 18, 19 and 35 read 另口 / 口 / 另工; comparison with a 군기시 sherd shows the correct reading is 另工.
정양모 noted that 관음리 yields 另, 口 and 二 rather than 左·右, and dated it before 1717.

rows.meaning: 'Second/third/fourth pottery (unit?)': unexplained numbered marks at 궁평리
rows.technique: incised inside the foot
rows.date_note: 궁평리 1·2호, dated 1684-1702 by the 甲子 and 壬午 ganji found with them (kkj2022).
rows.what_it_tells: A 궁평리 official-kiln mark of the 1680s-1700s.
rows.cautions: Meaning not explained in the sources.

facts.text: Excavation of 궁평리 1 and 2 produced ganji-incised sherds (甲子 1684) together with 二陶 and 三陶 marks; a 四陶 dish is in the Gyeonggi Ceramic Museum.
facts.quote: '甲子(1684)' 등 간지가 새겨진 음각명문과 함께 '二陶'

rows.meaning: Month-and-day numbers incised with the ganji (e.g. 五初三 = 5th month, 3rd day; 閏 = intercalary month)
rows.technique: incised through the glaze inside the foot next to 左/右 and the ganji
rows.date_note: First at 학동리 9호 (庚十十二, 1610); common 1650-1654 at 송정동 and 1675 at 신대리; numbers added from 1626-27 (kgh2013).
rows.what_it_tells: Gives the month and day (probably of glazing) in the year named by the ganji; 송정동 dates show firing from the 3rd to the 10th month.
rows.cautions: The numbers were first thought to be firing quantities; 初 and 閏 show they are dates. 閏 only fits years with an intercalary month, which helps choose the cycle.

facts.text: 乙卯閏五十八 is read as the 18th day of the intercalary 5th month of 乙卯 (1675), and 五初三壬辰 as the 3rd day of the 5th month of 壬辰 (1652).
The numbers incised with a ganji are taken to mean the month and day of production.
Numbers were added to 左·右 + ganji from 1626-27.
庚十十二右 from 학동리 9호 is read as the 12th day of the 10th month of 庚戌 (1610).

rows.meaning: 'Office': read as 司饔(院) (Royal Kitchen Office) or 司膳(署)
rows.technique: stamped (인각) or incised inside the foot / on the interior
rows.where_on_object: interior base or inside the foot
rows.date_note: From the 우산리 kiln site, which operated in the 15th-16th centuries (songyi_gmc).
rows.what_it_tells: Official-kiln ware made for use in a government office (the Saongwon or Saseonseo).
rows.cautions: Single catalogue source; the full office name is not written.

facts.text: A dish from the 우산리 kiln site has 司 stamped; catalogue entries read it as 司饔 or 司膳 and take the ware to be for office use (기증2-976, 기증1-93).
The Saongwon's own porcelain seal (白磁 司饔院印, 2nd half 18th c., Kansong Art Museum, Treasure) is a seal, not a ware mark.
facts.quote: 사옹원(司饔院)에서 사용하기 위해 만든 백자인장

rows.meaning: 'King' (also 士 'scholar/officer', 殿 'hall'): rare single characters taken to name a royal or office user
rows.technique: incised
rows.where_on_object: interior base or inside the foot
rows.date_note: From the 우산리 kiln site (15th-16th c.).
rows.what_it_tells: Early official-kiln ware for a specific royal or official user.
rows.cautions: Single catalogue source; no published discussion found.

facts.text: Rare incised marks 王, 士, 太一殿, 殿 and (stamped) 司 occur on the interior or inside the foot of 우산리 kiln wares and are taken to name royal or office users.
facts.quote: 王, 士, 太一殿, 殿, 司 등 음각명문

rows.meaning: Hall of the Taoist deity Taeil (Great Unity), a state ritual office
rows.technique: inlaid (상감) on a stand; incised on kiln sherds
rows.date_note: Kwon Sohyun dates the NMK inlaid cup and stand to c.1434-1478, when the Taeiljeon at 의성 was active.
rows.what_it_tells: Ritual ware made for the Taeiljeon; the only inscribed Joseon inlaid white porcelain apart from epitaph tablets.
rows.cautions: Place of use (palace or regional Taeiljeon) is debated.

facts.text: The inlaid white porcelain cup and stand bequeathed by Lee Hong-kun to the National Museum of Korea is inscribed Taeiljeon and dated c.1434-1478.
facts.quote: only extant example of Joseon inlaid

facts.text: 太一殿 is also among the rare incised marks on 우산리 kiln wares.
facts.quote: 太一殿, 殿, 司 등 음각명문

facts.text: 太一殿 occurs as an inscription on 15th-century white porcelain, both inlaid (NMK cup stand) and incised (우산리 kiln sherds).

rows.meaning: 'Place (of use)': mark of the Naesusa (內需司), the king's private treasury
rows.technique: incised, or written in underglaze iron-brown, on the base
rows.date_note: Naesusa potters made 大·中·世·處 wares from c.1464; Naesusa firing stopped c.1501 (kgh2021); Kim Yunjeong calls the Seoul sherds 16th century.
rows.what_it_tells: Royal private (內用) ware of the late 15th-early 16th century, distinct from Saongwon 天地玄黃 ware.
rows.cautions: Dating of individual sherds is approximate.

facts.text: Naesusa ware was marked 處, meaning the royal household unit where it was used, whereas Saongwon ware bore Thousand Character Classic marks.
Naesusa potters are thought to have made wares marked 大, 中, 世 and 處 around 1464.
Two 16th-century white porcelain sherds from 세종로 have 處 on the base, one incised and one in underglaze iron-brown.

rows.meaning: 'Great': for 大殿 (the king's quarters) or a Naesusa category; 上 'upper' similarly
rows.technique: incised or stippled on the base
rows.date_note: Naesusa 大·中·世 from c.1464 (kgh2021); 大 and 上 stippled on a dish used before 1583 (kim_yunjeong2017).
rows.what_it_tells: Royal-household ware; 上·大 indicate the king's quarters.
rows.cautions: 19th-century 大 in underglaze blue is a different mark (see dae-19c).

facts.text: 大, 中, 世 and 處 are taken as Naesusa marks of c.1464.
On a dish stippled 이셩 (Prince Uian, before 1583) the stippled 上 and 大 mean 'upper' and 'big' and suggest the dish was first used in the king's quarters (大殿).

rows.meaning: 'Sacrifice / ritual': marks a vessel for ancestral or state rites (祭器 = ritual vessel)
rows.technique: written or incised on everyday dishes; 祭器 painted in underglaze iron at 송정동; hangul 졔긔 stippled
rows.date_note: 祭 alone on dishes occurs throughout the 16th-18th centuries (songyi_gmc); hangul 졔긔 on 16th-century palace sherds with 天/地 (kim_yunjeong2017).
rows.what_it_tells: The dish was set aside for rites; often an ordinary tableware form.
rows.cautions: A 祭 mark does not identify which shrine; from 1792 royal shrines marked ritual vessels systematically (kwak2016).

facts.text: Ritual dishes with 祭 alone written on everyday forms appear throughout the 16th-18th centuries; an iron-painted 祭器 cup from 송정동 (1649-54) is unusual in naming the vessel type.
Hangul 졔긔 and 허니 are old transcriptions of 祭器 (ritual vessel) and 獻彛 (ritual ewer); vessels so stippled, often also incised 天 or 地, date to the 16th century.
In 1792 marking of ritual vessels was made official policy; single-character marks on late-Joseon ritual wares name the shrine, and stippled year inscriptions record renewal.

rows.meaning: 'Tea bottle (offered) to the king'
rows.technique: written in iron-brown (石間朱) on the body before firing
rows.date_note: Ordered while the future Yeongjo was 都提調 of the Bunwon, before his accession in 1724, as recalled in an audience of 1727 (sjw_1727); museum date 1720s.
rows.what_it_tells: Official-kiln (pre-분원리) tribute bottle of the 1710s-1720s; the inscription was meant to stop theft of royal bottles.
rows.cautions: Two bottles are recorded (해강도자미술관, H 39.5 cm; NMK 건희2800, H 38.7 cm): possibly different items. The e-museum record lists the material as celadon, apparently an error.

facts.text: In 1727 李敏躋 recalled that at the Bunwon the tea bottles were inscribed 燔進上茶甁 in 石間朱 iron pigment; the king replied that this dated from his time before accession.
facts.quote: 以石間朱, 書燔進上茶甁四字

facts.text: The inscription was ordered to prevent Bunwon officials misappropriating royal wares; a bottle so inscribed is dated 1710s-1720s.
facts.quote: 석간주(石間朱)로 진상다병(進上茶甁)이라 쓰게

rows.meaning: Porcelain epitaph tablet (written with the dead person's name and dates) — the main dating anchors for kiln sites
rows.technique: incised, iron-brown or underglaze-blue writing; some plate-shaped with a base ganji
rows.date_note: Earliest dated iron-brown example c.1468 (Jeong Seon); kiln-site tablets 1542-1572 anchor the 16th-century kiln sequence (kkj2012).
rows.what_it_tells: A dated tablet found at a kiln site dates that kiln; a family tablet dates the year of burial.
rows.cautions: A tablet gives the burial year, which can be later than the death (e.g. re-burials, 1558). Tablets were special orders, so a tablet from a kiln dates the kiln's activity, not every ware there.

facts.text: The earliest dated underglaze iron-brown white porcelain is the epitaph plaque of 鄭善 (Grand Supervisor at the 尙膳監, d.1468), Haegang Ceramics Museum.

Epitaphs found at kiln sites date the 16th-century kilns: 우산리 9호 壬寅 (1542), 무갑리 14호 嘉靖二十七年 (1548), 번천리 9호 嘉靖壬子 (1552) and a re-burial tablet of 1558, 번천리 5호 嘉靖三十三年 (1554), 곤지암리 1호 underglaze-blue 隆慶六 (1572).
The 우산리 kiln site yielded an epitaph sherd dated 嘉靖 癸巳 (1533) according to the Gyeonggi Ceramic Museum catalogue.
NMK holds plate-shaped epitaph tablets of Prince Inheung's children with base ganji 丙右 (1626) and 丁卯 (1627), and a 丙午 (1606) plate for his first son, all official-kiln products.

rows.meaning: 'Eighth month of the 乙丑 year' on a square clay rod (kiln tool)
rows.technique: incised
rows.date_note: 乙丑 = 1445 or 1505; the 1964-65 NMK excavation of 도마리 1호 used it to date the kiln (kkj2012).
rows.what_it_tells: Dates the 도마리 1호 official kiln (天地玄黃 period) to 1445 or c.1505.
rows.cautions: 60-year ambiguity unresolved in the sources (1445 or 1505).

facts.text: A square clay rod incised 乙丑八月 from 도마리 kiln 1 dates the kiln to around 1445 or 1505.

rows.technique: incised through the glaze inside the foot, usually with 左, 右 or 別 and sometimes month-day numbers
rows.date_note: Kiln 정지리 (亭支里) kiln 3, operating c.1595-1603 (kkj2022); 1598-1605 (윤용이, per kkj2010).
rows.what_it_tells: Attributed to the Saongwon official kiln at 정지리 (亭支里) kiln 3, 1602; 左/右 name the production team, 別 extra (special-order) ware.
rows.cautions: A sexagenary year repeats every 60 years: the same characters also fit 1482, 1542, 1662, 1722. The year given here rests on the kiln (or consumption-site) context, foot shape and firing supports, not on the characters alone. Only the stem 壬 is written.

facts.text: Kiln 3 at 정지리 yielded a sherd incised 壬右, read as 壬寅 (1602); matching 壬左 and 壬右 sherds were found at 청진 8 and 청진 2-3 in Seoul.
Only 壬 is written; 1592 (壬辰) and 1612 (壬子) were rejected because ganji marks start only after the Imjin War (1592-98) and firing was halted in 1604-05.

rows.what_it_tells: The item was kept in the dowager queen's kitchen; the move of the inscription from base to lower body and the addition of a cyclical year help date it.
rows.cautions: Stippled inscriptions were added after firing, at the place of use, so they record ownership/use, not the kiln. Read archaic spellings as written (ᄉᆞ, 뎐, 쇼). Older literature read 쇼 as 所 'place'; Kim Yunjeong reads it as 燒(廚房).

facts.text: Inscriptions beginning 웃 relate to the queen dowager; 쇼 is 燒, short for 燒廚房 (royal kitchen), not 所.
From the 18th century the dowager's kitchen was split into outer (밧쇼) and inner (안쇼) kitchens, and in the second half of the 18th century cyclical years were added (정미 웃뎐안쇼 1787, 무오 웃밧쇼 1798).

Stippled inscriptions in Seoul fall off in the 17th-18th centuries and rise again in the 19th; after the 18th century they are mostly hangul and name the owner, with year, size and quantity added step by step.
facts.quote: 소유처에 간지(⼲⽀), 크기, 수량 등의 정보가

facts.text: A sherd stippled 웃안쇼 is in the National Museum of Korea (신수52040).
Hangul inscriptions were generally added after manufacture and transport, at the place of use; stippling was used on fully glazed fine ware and ink on the unglazed feet of coarse stacked ware.

rows.meaning: The queen dowager's private store (本宮 / 私藏) or maiden home (私第)

rows.date_note: 16th c.; accompanied by incised 地, 黃, 右 (kim_yunjeong2017).
rows.what_it_tells: 16th-century royal ware treated as the queen dowager's private property.
rows.cautions: Stippled inscriptions were added after firing, at the place of use, so they record ownership/use, not the kiln. Read archaic spellings as written (ᄉᆞ, 뎐, 쇼).

facts.text: 웃궁 and 웃졔 refer to the queen dowager's private store and maiden home; sherds are also incised 地, 黃 or 右.

rows.meaning: Royal kitchen of the Daejeon (大殿), the king's quarters; 신대쇼 = kitchen of the 'new' king's quarters

rows.date_note: 16th c. with 地/左; 17th c. with 別甲戌 (1634) and 左 乙八十; 신대쇼 after the court moved to Changdeokgung in 1611 (kim_yunjeong2017).
rows.what_it_tells: Ware used in the king's kitchen.
rows.cautions: Stippled inscriptions were added after firing, at the place of use, so they record ownership/use, not the kiln. Read archaic spellings as written (ᄉᆞ, 뎐, 쇼).

facts.text: 대쇼 refers to the royal kitchen of the Daejeon; 신대쇼 to the new king's quarters at Changdeokgung after 1611.

rows.meaning: Royal kitchen of the 'big hall' (큰뎐 = 大殿, the king's quarters); 큰밧쇼 = its outer kitchen
rows.technique: stippled (點刻/정각: dots chipped into the fired glaze with a point, after firing); also ink
rows.where_on_object: base; later body next to the foot
rows.date_note: 16th c. (with 天/黃); 큰밧쇼 17th c.; 계미 큰밧쇼 = 1763 (kim_yunjeong2017).
rows.what_it_tells: Ware of the king's kitchen; five 큰쇼 sherds at the 회암사 temple site are linked to Queen Munjeong's patronage (1565).
rows.cautions: Stippled inscriptions were added after firing, at the place of use, so they record ownership/use, not the kiln. Read archaic spellings as written (ᄉᆞ, 뎐, 쇼).

facts.text: 큰쇼 is the kitchen of the 큰뎐 (king's quarters); 큰밧쇼 its outer kitchen; a 계미 큰밧쇼 sherd from 경희궁 dates to 1763.

rows.meaning: Kitchen of the crown prince's quarters (東宮); 동뱟쇼 = its outer kitchen
rows.technique: stippled (點刻/정각: dots chipped into the fired glaze with a point, after firing)
rows.where_on_object: base (16th c.); body next to the foot (17th-18th c.)
rows.date_note: 16th c. with 天/右; 17th and 18th c. examples (kim_yunjeong2017).
rows.what_it_tells: Ware of the crown prince's household.
rows.cautions: Stippled inscriptions were added after firing, at the place of use, so they record ownership/use, not the kiln. Read archaic spellings as written (ᄉᆞ, 뎐, 쇼). DISPUTED: Park Jungmin (2012) glosses 동소 as an 'eastern office' rather than the crown prince's kitchen.

facts.text: 동쇼 refers to the kitchen of the crown prince's quarters (Donggung), 동뱟쇼 to its outer kitchen.
Park Jungmin's abstract glosses 동소 as the eastern office.

rows.meaning: Inner kitchen of the royal grandson's (世孫宮) quarters
rows.technique: stippled (點刻/정각: dots chipped into the fired glaze with a point, after firing)
rows.date_note: First half of the 18th c. per kim_yunjeong2017.
rows.what_it_tells: Ware of the royal grandson's household (18th century).
rows.cautions: Stippled inscriptions were added after firing, at the place of use, so they record ownership/use, not the kiln. Read archaic spellings as written (ᄉᆞ, 뎐, 쇼).

facts.text: A bowl stippled 셰손궁 안쇼 from the 경희궁 gate-bridge site was used in the inner kitchen of the royal grandson's quarters.
The National Museum of Korea holds a Jongno sherd catalogued '셰숀궁안쇼' (신수52049).

rows.meaning: Hyebingung (惠嬪宮), household of Lady Hyegyeong, widow of Crown Prince Sado
rows.technique: stippled (點刻/정각: dots chipped into the fired glaze with a point, after firing)
rows.date_note: Title used 1762/63 to 1776 (then 惠慶宮); the household returned to Changdeokgung in 1763.1 (choi2013); 갑오 = 1774 (kim_yunjeong2017).
rows.what_it_tells: A tightly datable 18th-century stippled mark (1763-1776) on fine Bunwon-ri ware fired without saggars.
rows.cautions: Stippled inscriptions were added after firing, at the place of use, so they record ownership/use, not the kiln. Read archaic spellings as written (ᄉᆞ, 뎐, 쇼).

facts.text: 혜빙궁 inscriptions date from January 1763 to March 1776 from the title changes in the Veritable Records; 안쇼 = inner kitchen.
A dish sherd stippled 갑오 혜빙궁ᄉᆡᆼ from the 어영청 site dates to 1774.

rows.meaning: Sujingung (壽進宮), a royal private treasury and shrine palace
rows.technique: stippled (點刻/정각: dots chipped into the fired glaze with a point, after firing)
rows.date_note: Sherd dated 17th c. (kim_yunjeong2017).
rows.what_it_tells: Ware of one of the 'one office and four palaces' (一司四宮) private royal treasuries.
rows.cautions: Stippled inscriptions were added after firing, at the place of use, so they record ownership/use, not the kiln. Read archaic spellings as written (ᄉᆞ, 뎐, 쇼).

facts.text: A 17th-century sherd stippled 슈진궁 from 청진 2-3 was used at Sujingung, the private treasury of the (grand) queen dowager.

rows.meaning: Probably 中宮 (the queen's quarters), in an archaic spelling
rows.technique: stippled
rows.date_note: Undated in the catalogue; 신묘 is a cyclical year (1651/1711/1771/1831/1891).
rows.what_it_tells: Ware of the queen's household.
rows.cautions: Reading 듕궁 = 中宮 is ours; the catalogue gives no gloss. Stippled inscriptions were added after firing, at the place of use, so they record ownership/use, not the kiln. Read archaic spellings as written (ᄉᆞ, 뎐, 쇼).

facts.text: The National Museum of Korea holds a Jongno sherd catalogued '신묘교듕궁안진지겻' (신수52047).

rows.meaning: Jinjeon, a royal portrait hall (identified with 璿源殿)
rows.technique: stippled (點刻/정각: dots chipped into the fired glaze with a point, after firing)
rows.date_note: 16th c. (kim_yunjeong2017).
rows.what_it_tells: Ritual ware of the royal portrait hall.
rows.cautions: Stippled inscriptions were added after firing, at the place of use, so they record ownership/use, not the kiln. Read archaic spellings as written (ᄉᆞ, 뎐, 쇼).

facts.text: 진젼 refers to the royal portrait hall where the kings' portraits were enshrined.

rows.meaning: Ancestral shrine (祠堂); 반빗간 = its kitchen
rows.technique: stippled (點刻/정각: dots chipped into the fired glaze with a point, after firing)
rows.date_note: 16th c. (kim_yunjeong2017).
rows.what_it_tells: Ritual ware of a royal shrine.
rows.cautions: Stippled inscriptions were added after firing, at the place of use, so they record ownership/use, not the kiln. Read archaic spellings as written (ᄉᆞ, 뎐, 쇼).

facts.text: ᄉᆞ당 or ᄉᆞ당 반빗간 refers to a ritual facility where royal ancestral tablets were enshrined.

rows.meaning: Sogyeokseo (昭格署), the Taoist ritual office
rows.technique: stippled (點刻/정각: dots chipped into the fired glaze with a point, after firing)

rows.what_it_tells: Ware used at the Taoist ritual office before 1592.
rows.cautions: Stippled inscriptions were added after firing, at the place of use, so they record ownership/use, not the kiln. Read archaic spellings as written (ᄉᆞ, 뎐, 쇼).

facts.text: Vessels stippled 쇼격 were used at the Sogyeokseo between 1522 and 1592.
facts.quote: was used between 1522 and the launch

rows.meaning: Personal names or titles of princes and princesses (e.g. 혜슌 = Princess Hyesun 惠順翁主)
rows.technique: stippled (點刻/정각: dots chipped into the fired glaze with a point, after firing)
rows.where_on_object: base (16th c.); body next to the foot (18th c.)
rows.date_note: Each name dates an item to the years the child lived in the palace: 혜슌 before 1522, 영양 c.1532, 덕흥 1538-42, 졍신 1526-52, 이셩 before 1583, 뎡신 before 1593, 연령군 1703-08, 화슌 1725-32 (kim_yunjeong2017).
rows.what_it_tells: Unusually precise dates for palace ware; the vessel was used in that child's quarters before marriage or departure.
rows.cautions: Stippled inscriptions were added after firing, at the place of use, so they record ownership/use, not the kiln. Read archaic spellings as written (ᄉᆞ, 뎐, 쇼). 화영옹쥬 and 쳥근현쥬 (NMK sherds) are not identified in the sources consulted.

facts.text: Names of four children of Jungjong, two of Seonjo, one of Sukjong and one of Yeongjo are stippled on palace white porcelain, used in their quarters before they left the palace.
facts.quote: in the living quarters of the princes

facts.text: The National Museum of Korea holds Jongno sherds catalogued '화영옹쥬겻쥬방' (신수52048) and '쳥근현쥬겻' (신수52045).

rows.meaning: 'Ritual (祭) — 돈동' (a place or household name; not glossed)

rows.date_note: Catalogued only as Joseon.
rows.what_it_tells: A household ritual dish marked in hangul.

facts.text: The National Hangeul Museum holds a white porcelain ritual dish with the hangul '졔 돈동' (한구7298).

rows.meaning: 'Jar of the household of Mr Kim of Nakdong (駱洞)'
rows.technique: written in iron-brown
rows.date_note: 19th c. (bang_km32).

rows.cautions: Single source.

facts.text: A jar has '낙동김셔방댁항' written in brown iron oxide on the base, a Seoul gentry household's storage jar of the 19th century.

rows.meaning: 'At the time of the royal wedding' (嘉禮時)
rows.technique: stippled around or inside the foot
rows.where_on_object: around the foot or inside the foot
rows.date_note: Pattern: cyclical year + 가례시 + place (큰뎐 etc.) + 고간 + size + quantity (choi2020).
rows.what_it_tells: Identifies ware supplied for a specific 19th-century royal wedding.
rows.cautions: Stippled after firing; datable only through the cyclical year plus the named wedding. Fourteen wedding items are known (choi2020); all are saggar-fired quality Bunwon-ri ware.

facts.text: Wedding inscriptions follow the pattern year + 가례(길례) + place of use + size + quantity, stippled around or inside the foot.
A 1866 jar has the stippled wedding inscription around the foot and a blue 大 inside it.

rows.meaning: '丁酉 (1837) royal wedding, Great Hall storeroom …' — Queen Hyohyeon's wedding to Heonjong
rows.technique: stippled
rows.date_note: 丁酉 + 가례 = Heonjong's wedding of 1837; 큰뎐 = 대조전, Changdeokgung (choi2020).
rows.what_it_tells: Made for the 1837 wedding banquet.
rows.cautions: Stippled after firing; datable only through the cyclical year plus the named wedding. Fourteen wedding items are known (choi2020); all are saggar-fired quality Bunwon-ri ware. 이뉴 is unexplained.

facts.text: Bowls inscribed 뎡유가례시큰뎐고간… (Ewha Womans University Museum; Seoul Museum of History) were used at Queen Hyohyeon's 1837 wedding; 큰뎐 is Daejojeon.

rows.meaning: '저동궁 (苧洞宮), princess's wedding, temporary banquet kitchen …' — Princess Deokon's wedding, 1837
rows.technique: stippled

rows.what_it_tells: Made for Princess Deokon's 1837 wedding.
rows.cautions: Stippled after firing; datable only through the cyclical year plus the named wedding. Fourteen wedding items are known (choi2020); all are saggar-fired quality Bunwon-ri ware.

facts.text: Bowls and dishes stippled 뎌동궁길례시슉셜쇼… (Ewha Womans University Museum; Haegang) belong to Princess Deokon's 1837 wedding.

rows.meaning: '甲辰 (1844) royal wedding, Great Hall storeroom, medium size, 70 jук'
rows.technique: stippled
rows.date_note: Queen Hyojeong's wedding, 1844; 큰뎐 = 광명전, Gyeonghuigung (choi2020).
rows.what_it_tells: Made for the 1844 wedding.
rows.cautions: Stippled after firing; datable only through the cyclical year plus the named wedding. Fourteen wedding items are known (choi2020); all are saggar-fired quality Bunwon-ri ware.

facts.text: A blue-and-white 福-character dish in the National Museum of Korea is stippled 갑진가례시큰뎐고간듕쇼칠십듁 (1844).

rows.meaning: '丁未 (1847) royal wedding, Sunhwagung storeroom …' — wedding of Royal Consort Gyeongbin Kim
rows.technique: stippled
rows.date_note: Consort Gyeongbin's wedding, 1847; 순화궁 = her palace title (choi2020).
rows.what_it_tells: Part of Consort Gyeongbin's wedding goods stored at her residence (Nakseonjae per choi2020).
rows.cautions: Stippled after firing; datable only through the cyclical year plus the named wedding. Fourteen wedding items are known (choi2020); all are saggar-fired quality Bunwon-ri ware. Choi revised her 1996 view that 순화궁 was Gyeongbin's birth home.

facts.text: Bowls and dishes stippled 뎡미가례시순화궁고간… are in the National Museum of Korea and the Metropolitan Museum (2010.174, dated 1847).
A National Palace Museum bowl (고궁3998) is stippled '뎡미가례시 슌화궁 고간 일듁'.

rows.meaning: '戊申 (1848), Sugangjae (壽康齋) storeroom, medium size, 20 jук'
rows.technique: stippled
rows.where_on_object: around the outside of the foot
rows.date_note: Dated 1848 by the museum (npmk).
rows.what_it_tells: Ware stored at Sugangjae, Changdeokgung.
rows.cautions: Single source; the museum page renders archaic syllables with private-use glyphs.

facts.text: A National Palace Museum dish (고궁588) is stippled 무신슈강[ᄌᆡ]고간듕쇼이십듁 and dated 1848; the place is 수강재.

rows.meaning: '壬子 year, Great Hall storeroom, 4 jук'
rows.technique: stippled

rows.what_it_tells: Royal ware of the mid-19th century.

facts.text: Busan Museum's bowl (구입10202) is stippled 임자큰뎐고간사듁 and dated to probably 1852; the National Palace Museum's 고궁53 has 임자큰뎐고간사□□, also put at 1852.

rows.meaning: '丙寅 (1866) royal wedding, Great Hall storeroom, large-medium-small, 20 jук' — Queen Myeongseong's wedding

facts.text: 壽福 jars in the National Palace Museum (고궁54, 고궁597) have blue 大 inside the foot and the stippled 병인가례시큰뎐고간… around it (1866).

rows.meaning: '丁巳 year, Yeongchunheon (迎春軒) storeroom …'

rows.what_it_tells: Royal ware for a hall of Changdeokgung.
rows.cautions: Year unresolved; single source.

facts.text: National Palace Museum dishes (창덕413, 창덕455, 창덕357) carry stippled 뎡사영츈헌고간… or 뎡사읏뎐고간… with 別進 in blue.

rows.meaning: '己亥 year, Great Hall storeroom …'
rows.technique: stippled (釘刻)
rows.date_note: 己亥 = 1779, 1839 or 1899 (our arithmetic; museum gives none).
rows.what_it_tells: Royal ware.
rows.cautions: Year unresolved; single source.

facts.text: A National Palace Museum dish (창덕223) is stippled 긔해큰뎐고간대듕쇼이십듁.
facts.quote: 白磁靑畵긔해釘刻銘壽字文楪匙

rows.meaning: 'Great Hall' — the main hall where a royal wedding banquet was held, or the king's quarters (大殿)
rows.technique: stippled
rows.date_note: Common in 18th-19th-c. stippled inscriptions (kim_yunjeong2017; choi2020).
rows.what_it_tells: Royal ware; which building is meant depends on the wedding/year.
rows.cautions: DISPUTED gloss: museums gloss it as 大殿; choi2020 identifies it as the hall of the wedding feast (대조전 1837, 광명전 1844, 중희당 1866).

facts.text: In the 19th century the stippled 큰밧쇼 was replaced by 큰뎐고간 with a cyclical year.
In the wedding inscriptions 큰뎐 is the building where the 동뢰연 was held.
큰뎐 (with 고간 and a cyclical year) is the usual place term in 19th-century stippled court inscriptions.

rows.meaning: Storeroom (庫間)
rows.technique: stippled
rows.date_note: 19th-c. inscriptions.

rows.meaning: Unit of ten vessels (죽, written 竹)
rows.technique: stippled
rows.date_note: 19th-c. inscriptions.
rows.what_it_tells: Quantity in the issued set.

rows.meaning: Large, medium, small (大中小): size grade
rows.technique: stippled
rows.date_note: 19th-c. inscriptions.

rows.meaning: Read by the National Palace Museum as 大殿, the king's hall

facts.text: Blue-and-white bowls and dishes have 大 written in blue inside the foot, which the museum reads as 大殿.
The 1866 wedding jars combine a blue 大 inside the foot with the stippled wedding inscription.

rows.meaning: 'Upper chamber': royal (king's) use
rows.technique: underglaze blue
rows.date_note: Late 19th c. (npmk).
rows.what_it_tells: Royal-use Bunwon-ri ware.
rows.cautions: Single source; the museum glosses it both as 大殿 use and as 御用器.

facts.text: 上室 in blue inside the foot is glossed by the National Palace Museum as marking royal use (御用器) or Daejeon use.

rows.meaning: 'Offered': tribute (進上) ware for the court
rows.technique: underglaze blue
rows.date_note: Produced in quantity at Bunwon-ri in the late 19th to early 20th century (npmk), i.e. also after privatization.
rows.what_it_tells: Court tribute ware from Bunwon-ri, including the 분원공소 period.

facts.text: 進 in blue inside the foot marks tribute ware; such dishes were made in quantity at Bunwon-ri in the late 19th-early 20th century.
facts.quote: 진상(進上)용 그릇임을 알 수 있다

facts.text: The National Museum of Korea also holds a 「進」 dish (건희2494).

The Bunwon stopped being a full official kiln after the economies list (減省別單) of the 29th day of the 12th lunar month of 1882; it became the semi-official, semi-private 분원공소 (1883-1895), which still supplied court tribute ware.
Other accounts date the conversion to the 분원공소 to 1884, the year of its rules book 『分院磁器貢所節目』.
facts.quote: 분원 공소(貢所)로 전환되고 사실상 민영화될

rows.meaning: 'Special offering': probably special-order (別燔) tribute ware
rows.technique: underglaze blue
rows.date_note: 19th c.
rows.what_it_tells: High-grade special-order Bunwon-ri ware for the court.
rows.cautions: Reading 別進 = 別燔 + 進上 is ours; the museum's claim of firing above 1,300°C is unverified.

facts.text: 別進 dishes are described as specially fired high-temperature wares.
In the 1880s-90s court ware was priced as 元進上, 例燔 and 別燔; 別燔 were extra orders (e.g. royal weddings), usually blue-and-white or saggar-fired fine ware.
facts.quote: 年例元進上器皿과 内出別燔

rows.meaning: Single characters in underglaze blue on 19th-century court ware; meanings not established
rows.technique: underglaze blue
rows.where_on_object: inside the foot (中 安 典 淸 延); interior well (內 祥)
rows.date_note: 19th c.; one 淸 dish is dated modern (근현대) by the museum.
rows.what_it_tells: Court ware of the 19th century; the place of use is not known.
rows.cautions: The museum guesses 延 = 延生殿 or 延吉堂 and 祥 = ritual use; kwak2016 argues single characters on late-Joseon ritual ware name shrines. Unresolved.

facts.text: The National Palace Museum holds 19th-century blue-and-white dishes with single blue characters 中, 安, 典, 淸 or 延 inside the foot and 內 or 祥 in the well.
facts.quote: 白磁靑畵中字銘壽字文楪匙

facts.text: Single-character marks on late-Joseon ritual vessels name the shrine, to keep vessels from being mixed up.
facts.quote: 한 글자 명문은 사당의 호를 지칭

rows.meaning: Unhyeongung, residence of the Heungseon Daewongun (father of Gojong)
rows.technique: underglaze blue
rows.date_note: Second half of the 19th c. because of the residence (bang_km32); its typical lingzhi-and-grass motif appears in Gyeongbokgung layers ending before 1890 (choi2013).
rows.what_it_tells: Bunwon-ri ware ordered for the Daewongun's household, second half of the 19th century.

facts.text: 雲峴 wares are datable to the second half of the 19th century because Unhyeongung was the Daewongun's residence; the mark occurs on dishes, jars and bowls.
The National Palace Museum and National Museum of Korea hold items with 운현 in blue on the base.
The lingzhi-and-grass motif typical of 운현 items occurs only in Gyeongbokgung layers dated before 1890.
facts.quote: ‘운현’의 명문이 있는 유물에서 쉽게 볼 수 있는 영지초화문

rows.meaning: Household of Princess Sukseon (淑善翁主, 1793-1836), daughter of Jeongjo
rows.technique: underglaze blue
rows.date_note: Princess Sukseon's lifetime (encykorea_idonggung).
rows.what_it_tells: Ware of a princess's household, early 19th century.
rows.cautions: Writing is crude.

facts.text: A small square jar in the National Palace Museum has 履洞宮 in blue on the base, the household of Princess Sukseon.

rows.meaning: 'Longevity and good fortune': auspicious characters, usually decoration
rows.technique: underglaze blue (regular or seal script)
rows.where_on_object: interior well, outside wall; occasionally on the base rim
rows.date_note: Turned into motifs from the Jeongjo period; dominant on 19th-c. royal ware (bang_km32; choi2013; choi2020).
rows.what_it_tells: Typical of late-18th-19th-century Bunwon-ri ware; not a mark of maker or user.
rows.cautions: A 壽 in the well is decoration; a single character inside the foot is a mark. Also used on Chinese export wares.

facts.text: From the Jeongjo period 壽 and 福 were designed into motifs, in regular or seal script inside frames.
facts.quote: 수(壽)·복(福) 두 글자를 도안화하여 문양으로

facts.text: 壽福 characters and stylised flowers dominate the pre-1865 19th-century layers at Gyeongbokgung; 7 of the 14 wedding items carry them.

rows.meaning: 'Double happiness'
rows.technique: underglaze blue
rows.date_note: 19th c. on pipes and dishes (bang_km32).
rows.what_it_tells: Auspicious decoration of the 19th century.
rows.cautions: Does not prove Korean manufacture: the NMK holds a Qing bowl and a Joseon dish both with 囍.

facts.text: 19th-century blue-and-white tobacco pipes carry 囍.
The National Museum of Korea holds a Joseon 囍 dish (증6940) and a Qing 囍 bowl (증4030).

rows.meaning: Chinese imperial reign marks (Xianfeng 1851-61; Ming Xuande) copied on Joseon wares
rows.technique: underglaze blue
rows.date_note: 19th c. (bang_km32).
rows.what_it_tells: A Chinese reign mark on a Korean item is a 19th-century borrowing, not a date.
rows.cautions: Single source.

facts.text: A polygonal blue-and-white dish with 咸豊年制 and Joseon water-droppers and dishes with 大明宣德年製 show Chinese reign marks on 19th-century Korean wares.

rows.meaning: Plum-blossom emblem of the Korean Empire (1897-1910), later of the Yi royal house
rows.technique: mostly gold overglaze or decal on imported tableware; rarely blue or red painted
rows.date_note: Emblem cited as national in the 1900 decoration regulations (song2013); after 1907 the Yi house emblem.
rows.what_it_tells: Korean Empire court tableware, almost always made in Japan or France.
rows.cautions: Over 95% of surviving banquet ware is Japanese (Noritake, 日本陶器, 深川製磁, 日本硬質陶器) or French (Pillivuyt); the plum was sometimes added after import. Few items were made in Korea, because Bunwon had declined after privatization.

facts.text: Korean Empire plum-blossom ware had to be imported because Bunwon's industry had declined after privatization; over 95% of the banquet ware is Japanese or French.
facts.quote: 분원의 민영 이후 쇠락한 요업실태를 극복하지 못해 수입에 의존

facts.text: The 1900 decoration regulations call the plum the national emblem; after Gojong's abdication in 1907 it became the Yi house emblem.
A Pillivuyt item marked PARIS EXP 1900 has a worn plum, possibly added after manufacture, and an identical item has no plum.
After the 공소 failed, the 번자회사 (founded 1897) used the old Bunwon works with a head office at 광교 in Seoul; renamed 燔砂會社 it first made colored wares, and the 分院磁器株式會社 was founded in August 1910.
Japanese potters set up a kiln at Bunwon in 1904 and three Japanese potters worked there from 1906.

rows.meaning: 'Ninth year of Gwangmu' = 1905 (Korean Empire era name)
rows.technique: red overglaze enamel inside the foot; plum blossom in blue
rows.date_note: Era-name date (eom2023; npmk).
rows.what_it_tells: A dated Korean Empire item; possibly made by Chinese potters at Bunwon or ordered from China and decorated in Korea.
rows.cautions: Body and mark look Chinese; the maker is unresolved.

facts.text: A National Palace Museum dish and a sherd from the 무악2구역 site have a plum blossom and 光武九年 (1905) in red enamel inside the foot.

rows.meaning: Office of Palace Banquets (successor of the Saongwon from 1895)
rows.technique: gold overglaze with plum blossom and laurel
rows.date_note: Made by Nippon Koshitsu Toki (日本硬質陶器) 1908-1911 (eom2023); the office was reorganized from the Saongwon in 1895 (npmk).
rows.what_it_tells: Japanese-made Korean Empire banquet plates.
rows.cautions: Not Korean-made.

facts.text: 典膳司 plates with a plum blossom were made by 日本硬質陶器株式會社, 1908-1911.
The 典膳司 reorganized the former Saongwon in 1895.

rows.meaning: Nakseonjae, Changdeokgung residence used by the imperial family
rows.technique: underglaze blue
rows.where_on_object: under the plum in the well, or inside a double foot
rows.date_note: Korean Empire, 20th c. (npmk; eom2023).
rows.what_it_tells: Imperial family ware for small banquets.
rows.cautions: Maker not stated.

facts.text: Dishes with a plum blossom and 樂善齋 in blue are in the National Palace Museum.

rows.meaning: Office of the Yi Royal Household (colonial period, 1910-1945)
rows.technique: blue, written vertically
rows.date_note: Colonial-period office.
rows.what_it_tells: Japanese-made ware for the former royal household under colonial rule.
rows.cautions: Single source; not Korean-made.

facts.text: A 李王職 item in the National Palace Museum was made in Japan in the modern period.

rows.meaning: 'Hanyang (Seoul) Goryeo ware': a Japanese-run workshop in Seoul making Goryeo-style celadon reproductions in the colonial period.
rows.technique: Not documented in any source read: how (or whether) this maker marked its wares was not found.
rows.date_note: Founded August 1911 (Encykorea, Yu Geun-hyeong entry) or 1912 (Oh 2022). Owned by Tomita Gisaku from 1924 (Oh). No closing date found.
rows.what_it_tells: A ware, box or label naming this workshop is a colonial-period reproduction of Goryeo celadon made in Seoul for Japanese residents, tourists and dealers (the dealer Haesi Sanghoe; Mitsukoshi), not a Goryeo antique. It was where Yu Geun-hyeong and Hwang In-chun, the two best-known Korean revivers, learned the craft.
rows.cautions: Founder and founding year are disputed: Encykorea says Tomita Gisaku founded it in August 1911 at Mukjeong-dong; Oh (2022) says Umii Benzō founded it in 1912 at Higashi-shiken-chō (today's Jangchung-dong) and sold it to Tomita in 1924. Hwang In-chun is said to have entered it at 16, which (born 1894) would be c.1909-10, earlier than either founding date. The form of any mark is unknown, so a missing mark proves nothing, and once an item is separated from its box or label it can pass as Goryeo ware: the V&A bowl C.164-1926 was acquired as Goryeo and is now catalogued as a probable 20th-century Japanese imitation.

facts.text: Encykorea's Yu Geun-hyeong entry says Japanese businessman Tomita Gisaku founded the celadon workshop Hanyang Goryeo-so at Mukjeong-dong, Seoul, in August 1911.
facts.quote: 도미타 기사쿠가 1911년 8월에 설립한 청자공방 (the celadon workshop Tomita Gisaku founded in August 1911)

facts.text: Oh (2022) says Kanyō Kōraiyaki was set up in 1912 by Umii Benzō (b. 1875), owner of the Seoul souvenir dealer 海市商會, at Higashi-shiken-chō (today's Jangchung-dong); after his Tokyo branch was damaged in the 1923 Kantō earthquake, Umii sold it to Tomita Gisaku in 1924. (The English Wikipedia article repeats this; cross-check only.)
facts.quote: In 1912 Umii set up Kanyō Kōraiyaki

facts.text: The Seoul dealer Haesi Sanghoe (海市商會) had its ceramics made by Hanyang Goryeo-so (and its lacquer by 高麗髹), per a 1918 Pusan Ilbo article cited by Kim Se-rin; Oh independently describes the workshop as associated with the same dealer and run by its owner. Both rest partly on the same 1918 newspaper article.
facts.quote: 도자기는 한양고려소(漢陽高麗燒)…에서의 제작 (its ceramics were made at Hanyang Goryeo-so)

facts.text: Yu Geun-hyeong began learning ceramics at Hanyang Goryeo-so in 1911.
facts.quote: ‘한양고려소(漢陽高麗燒)’에서 일하면서 (while working at Hanyang Goryeo-so)

facts.text: Hwang In-chun also trained there, entering at age 16 according to Encykorea.
facts.quote: 16세에 일본인이 운영하던 청자공방 (at 16, a Japanese-run celadon workshop)

facts.text: By the mid-1910s the workshop exhibited at expositions in Tokyo and Seoul; Japan's Imperial Household Ministry bought items shown at Tokyo expositions in 1914 and 1917; Umii opened a Tokyo Nihonbashi branch selling its celadon in 1913.

Kanyō Kōraiyaki and Sanwa Kōraiyaki were the two main suppliers of Goryeo-style celadon to Mitsukoshi's Korean Product Showroom in Seoul (Oh, citing Yu Geun-hyeong's 1982 autobiography); Kanyō also supplied Mitsukoshi Tokyo's Oriental section from 1921.
Japanese residents in Korea came to control the making, supply and sale of reproduction celadon in the colonial period.
facts.quote: 재조선 일본인들이 독점하게 되면서 (as Japanese residents in Korea came to monopolise it)

facts.text: A V&A inlaid celadon bowl (C.164-1926) acquired as Goryeo is now catalogued as a probable 20th-century Japanese imitation, showing how such copies entered Western collections as antiques.

rows.meaning: 'Sanwa (Samhwa) Goryeo ware': Tomita Gisaku's celadon-reproduction workshop at Jinnampo (鎭南浦, Chinnamp'o), South Pyeongan, now North Korea.
wares: Goryeo-style inlaid celadon: vases, incense burners, cake dishes, sake cups and bottles, tea sets
celadon figures (a statue of Wang In)
rows.technique: Not documented in any source read: how (or whether) this maker marked its wares was not found.
rows.date_note: Hamada Yoshinori was invited in 1911 and the Government-General gave a start-up subsidy in 1912 (Oh); the MOMAT 2012 exhibition dated its items c.1911-1945. English Wikipedia gives 1908 for the founding (cross-check only, unsourced there). Continued by Tomita's son Tomita Seiichi after 1930.
rows.what_it_tells: An item, box or label naming Sanwa Kōraiyaki is a colonial-period (1910s-1940s) Japanese-made reproduction of Goryeo celadon from Jinnampo, sold as an affordable alternative to excavated Goryeo celadon, including through Tomita Shōkai and Mitsukoshi in Seoul. Its best products copied famous Goryeo items in the Yi Royal Household Museum.
rows.cautions: The workshop deliberately made faithful copies of Goryeo masterpieces (Oh), so an unmarked or label-less item can pass as Goryeo. How its wares were marked is not documented in the sources read; the Japanese literature (Okamoto 2008 in the Sannomaru Shōzōkan bulletin; Jung Eun-jin 2014, 2015, 2016, 2019) is where marks would be described and was not read. Hamada Yoshikatsu's death year differs: 1980 (Oh) vs 1975 (artscape/MOMAT).

facts.text: Sanwa Kōraiyaki was Tomita Gisaku's (1858-1930) Goryeo-celadon revival workshop at Jinnampo; Tomita went to Korea in 1899 and built his businesses (mining, farming, sericulture, banking) there.
facts.quote: 富田は1899（明治32）年に朝鮮に渡った (Tomita went to Korea in 1899)

facts.text: Tomita brought in the potter Hamada Yoshinori (1882-1920), from a Yatsushiro-ware family in Kumamoto and trained at the Arita Technical School, in 1911; his half-brother Yoshikatsu joined in 1915.
facts.quote: 熊本から濱田義徳（1882-1920）・美勝 (the Hamada brothers from Kumamoto)

facts.text: Hamada Yoshikatsu's (美勝) dates are given as 1895-1980 by Oh and 1895-1975 by the artscape review of the 2012 MOMAT exhibition.
The Government-General gave Sanwa Kōraiyaki a 1,000-yen start-up subsidy in 1912, and South Pyeongan province 700 yen a year for running costs.
facts.quote: a subsidy of 1000 yen for start-up costs

facts.text: By 1916 the Hamada brothers produced close copies of Goryeo celadon, including copies of the Yi Royal Household Museum's gourd-shaped ewer with inlaid grape-and-boy design and its openwork incense burner.

A 1925 price list of Sanwa wares sold at Tomita Shōkai gives vases at 3-150 yen, incense burners 1.5-25 yen, cake dishes 0.5-25 yen and tea sets 1.5-9 yen; annual production was worth 10,000 yen in 1924.
Sanwa inlaid celadon (a cake bowl and a vase, dated c.1911-1945) was shown in the 2012 MOMAT Crafts Gallery exhibition on Japanese craftsmen in Asia.
facts.quote: 三和高麗焼《青磁象嵌花瓶》c.1911-1945

facts.text: The workshop also made figures: Jung Eun-jin published a newly found Sanwa celadon statue of Wang In (王仁) in 2019 (title only seen).
facts.quote: 三和高麗焼「青磁王仁像」 (Sanwa ware 'celadon Wang In statue')

facts.text: After Tomita died in 1930 his son Tomita Seiichi continued the business.
facts.quote: his son Tomita Seiichi succeeded him

facts.text: The Imperial Household Agency's Sannomaru Shōzōkan published a study of Sanwa Kōraiyaki (Okamoto Takashi, 2008), indicating items in the Japanese imperial collections.
facts.quote: 三和高麗焼について (On Sanwa Kōrai-yaki)

rows.meaning: Hwang In-chun (1894-1950), Korean potter who ran the first Korean-owned Goryeo-celadon revival workshop, at Kaesong (開城).
rows.technique: Not documented in any source read: how (or whether) this maker marked its wares was not found.
rows.date_note: Oh (2022) dates his Korean-run workshop to the end of the 1920s (Chungoe Ilbo, 26 Nov 1929); Encykorea dates his Kaesong celadon institute to 1937. Died 19 Jan 1950 (Encykorea); a 1990 newspaper says 1949.
rows.what_it_tells: A rare name: only 11 surviving works are known (Encykorea), most from his Kaesong kiln period. He trained at Hanyang Goryeo-so and in Japan, and taught a generation of potters in Kaesong, including North Korea's leading celadon reproducer Woo Chi-seon and his son Hwang Jong-gu.
rows.cautions: No source describes how his wares were signed or marked. With only 11 known works, any item attributed to him needs provenance. Colonial Kaesong also had a Japanese-run ceramics research laboratory reproducing Goryeo celadon, where he worked as a contract engineer, so Kaesong origin alone does not mean his workshop.

facts.text: Hwang In-chun was born in 1894 and died in 1950.
He trained at the Japanese-run workshop Hanyang Goryeo-so.
facts.quote: 16세에 일본인이 운영하던 청자공방 (at 16, a Japanese-run celadon workshop)

facts.text: He studied ceramics in Japan from 1919 to 1923.
Oh says the only Korean-run Goryeo celadon revival workshop of the colonial period was set up at the end of the 1920s and that Hwang In-chun opened it (citing Chungoe Ilbo, 26 Nov 1929).
In 1937 he organized the Kaesong Ceramics Guild (開城制陶業組合) with Gyeonggi province and Kaesong city subsidies and opened a Goryeo Celadon Institute (高麗靑磁硏究所) at Seonjuk-dong, Kaesong.

He was a contract engineer for the colonial authorities' ceramics research in Kaesong: Encykorea names the Gyeonggi-do Industrial Laboratory; a 1990 Seoul Shinmun article describes a Japanese-founded ceramics materials laboratory in Kaesong set up to reproduce Goryeo celadon.
facts.quote: 경기도 공업시험소의 촉탁기술자 (contract engineer of the Gyeonggi Industrial Laboratory)

facts.text: His small Kaesong institute took about 20 boys as pupils in the late 1930s, among them Woo Chi-seon (later North Korea's leading celadon reproducer) and his son Hwang Jong-gu.
facts.quote: 20명 정도의 소년들을 문하에 (about 20 boys as pupils)

facts.text: Eleven works by him survive, all but one from his Kaesong kiln period.
facts.quote: 11점의 작품들은 … 개성요(開城窯) 시기 (11 works … Kaesong kiln period)

rows.meaning: Art Products Manufactory of the Yi Royal Household Agency: the royal craft workshop in Seoul (founded 1908 as the Hanseong Art Products Manufactory), making silver, metalwork, lacquer, ink, textiles and Goryeo-style celadon.
wares: silver and silver-plated brass (sinseollo, vases in Chinese ritual-bronze forms, cups)
rows.technique: Products carried the engraved royal plum-blossom emblem (李花) according to Encykorea; one silver set is recorded with the maker's inscription 京城李王家美術工場造; under the later company, printed paper labels (see separate rows). No dated sequence of stamps was found.
rows.where_on_object: emblem engraved on lid and body (silver); inscription position not recorded
rows.date_note: Founded October 1908 as 漢城美術品製作工場. The rename to 李王職美術品製作所 is dated December 1910 (Encykorea, silver bowl entry), 1911 (Encykorea, institution entry) or June 1913, when the Yi Royal Household Agency took it over (AKS sillokwiki; Oh 2022). Became the private Joseon Misulpum Jejakso Co. on 16 August 1922; dissolved 13 July 1936 (sillokwiki) or ran to about 1937 (Encykorea; Choi Bum).
rows.what_it_tells: An item credibly from this workshop was made in Seoul for the Korean imperial / Yi royal house or to be sold to (mostly Japanese) visitors and collectors, between 1908 and 1922; after 1922 the same works traded commercially as the Joseon Misulpum Jejakso.
rows.cautions: The plum-blossom emblem alone does not prove manufacture here: in 2023 the Cultural Heritage Administration deregistered a 'Yiwangjik' silver vase in the National Palace Museum after the 小林 stamp on its base showed it was made by Kobayashi Tokeiten in Tokyo. The founding funding is described differently (royal treasury in Encykorea; four Seoul merchants plus an interest-free royal loan in sillokwiki). Name forms vary in catalogues (李王家美術品製作所 at the Liang Yi Museum, which catalogues such silver as 'Japanese Silver').

facts.text: The workshop was founded in 1908 (October 1908 as 漢城美術品製作工場, per sillokwiki).
Sillokwiki says four Seoul merchants invested 10,000 won each with a 60,000-won interest-free loan from the imperial household; Encykorea says the royal house founded it from the privy purse.
facts.quote: 1908년에 이왕가에서 설립한 공예품 제작시설 (craft facility founded by the royal house in 1908)

facts.text: The rename to 이왕직미술품제작소 is dated June 1913, when the Yi Royal Household Agency took it over for 24,000 won.
Encykorea gives other dates for the rename: December 1910 (silver soup-bowl entry) and 1911 (institution entry).

On 16 August 1922 it became a private joint-stock company, the Joseon Misulpum Jejakso Co. (株式會社朝鮮美術品製作所), with management passing to Japanese investors; Tomita Gisaku was the second-largest shareholder after the Yi Royal Household.
facts.quote: 1922년 8월 16일에 주식회사 조직의 민간회사로 전환 (16 Aug 1922: became a joint-stock company)

facts.text: A ceramics department was added around 1910, and the workshop's Goryeo-style celadon was called 'Biwon ware' (秘苑磁器, after the palace Secret Garden).
Its buyers were mostly Japanese, who bought its products as souvenirs and gifts; under the company it turned increasingly to souvenirs.
facts.quote: 판매에 한층 적극적이 되면서 … 기념품 (more sales-minded … souvenirs)

facts.text: Encykorea says all its products were decorated with the plum-blossom (李花) emblem, and that the emblem continued to be engraved after 1910 for commercial reasons.
facts.quote: 모든 공예품에 장식되어 있다 (decorates all its crafts)

facts.text: Its metal department made royal silver sinseollo; a 1911 article reports a cheaper method of silver-plating brass bodies, also used for commercial sale.
facts.quote: 眞鍮製애 銀鍍金을施 (silver plating on brass)

facts.text: It supplied Korean wares to Mitsukoshi Tokyo's Oriental section when that opened in 1921.
facts.quote: Korean artefacts from the Yi Royal Household

variants: plum-blossom emblem of the Korean Empire / Yi royal house
rows.meaning: Plum (oyat) blossom: emblem of the Jeonju Yi royal house and national emblem of the Korean Empire, engraved or applied on royal silver, lacquer and other crafts.
rows.technique: engraved (음각), chased or applied as a device; not a written mark
rows.where_on_object: lid and body center on silver vessels (Encykorea, silver soup vessel)
rows.date_note: Emblem of the Korean Empire (1897-1910) and then of the Yi royal house; still used commercially after 1910 (Encykorea). The start year is the Empire's proclamation, given here for orientation, not from a source on marks.
rows.what_it_tells: Associates the item with the Korean imperial / Yi royal house: made for it, as a gift from it, or styled to look royal to be sold. It does not identify the maker.
rows.cautions: Not a maker's mark. A silver vase with this emblem in the National Palace Museum was registered in 2009 as Yiwangjik work and deregistered in 2023 when its 小林 base stamp showed it was made in Tokyo by Kobayashi Tokeiten; specialists called the assumption that any plum-blossom item is Yiwangjik work a clear error. The emblem was also used commercially after 1910.

facts.text: The plum blossom (李花) symbolises the Jeonju Yi royal house and was the national emblem of the Korean Empire; it is engraved on royal silver such as the National Palace Museum's silver soup vessel and silver cup.
facts.quote: 대한제국(大韓帝國)의 국장(國章)인 이화문 (the plum-blossom national emblem of the Korean Empire)

facts.text: Encykorea says it decorated all products of the Yiwangjik workshop and continued to be engraved after 1910 for commercial reasons.
facts.quote: 모든 공예품에 장식 (decorates all its crafts)

facts.text: In 2023 a silver vase with the emblem (銀製李花文花甁) was deregistered as a national heritage item because the 小林 stamp on its base showed it was made by Tokyo's Kobayashi Tokeiten; an specialist called the 'plum blossom = Yiwangjik' assumption a clear error.
facts.quote: '이화문이 있는 공예품은 이왕직미술품제작소 제작품'이라는 잘못된 인식 (the mistaken belief that plum-blossom crafts are Yiwangjik products)

rows.meaning: Stamp of Kobayashi Tokeiten (小林時計店), a Tokyo clock and art-goods maker that also made silver.
rows.technique: stamped (압인) on the base
rows.date_note: Firm active from the mid-19th century to 1943 (Yonhap, reporting the Cultural Heritage Administration).
rows.what_it_tells: Japanese (Tokyo) manufacture, even on silver bearing the Korean royal plum-blossom emblem; relevant because such items were made for, or given to, the Korean royal house and are easily mistaken for Seoul Yiwangjik work.
rows.cautions: Single source (a news report of the Cultural Heritage Administration's gazette notice, which was not read directly). The form of the stamp is not described beyond the two characters.

facts.text: The 小林 stamp on the base of a plum-blossom silver vase in the National Palace Museum identified it as a product of Kobayashi Tokeiten of Tokyo, which operated from the mid-19th century to 1943, made silver and supplied Japan's Imperial Household Ministry; the vase was deregistered in February 2023.

rows.meaning: 'Made by Haesi Sanghoe, Keijō (Seoul)': mark of a Japanese-owned Seoul souvenir and craft dealer that had its wares made by workshops.
rows.technique: written in ink (묵서) on the wooden box, with a seal (직인)
rows.date_note: Opened in 1906 (Kim) or 1908 at Honmachi (Oh) by Umii Benzō; Seoul head shop 1912; joint-stock company with a Tokyo head office from 1923; advertisements known to 1935 and the firm listed in 1937 (Kim).
rows.what_it_tells: A colonial-period souvenir retailer's mark (for Japanese residents and tourists). It names the seller, not necessarily the workshop that made the item.
rows.cautions: Dealer's mark: the dealer commissioned most of its wares, so the mark does not identify the actual maker. The only recorded example is on a box, and boxes can be separated from or swapped between items.

facts.text: Haesi Sanghoe was a Seoul shop selling Korean (and Chinese) local products, founded by Umii Benzō (海井辨藏, b. 1875); Kim dates the opening to 1906, Oh to 1908.
facts.quote: 우미이 벤조(海井辨藏: 1875‒?)가 1906년에 개업 (opened by Umii Benzō in 1906)

facts.text: It had its ceramics made by Hanyang Goryeo-so and its lacquer by 高麗髹, and sold Korean ceramics, lacquer and metalwork as souvenirs.
facts.quote: 판매 물품들을 공장에 위탁 제작 (had the goods it sold made by workshops)

facts.text: In 1923 it became a joint-stock company with a head office in Tokyo, managed in Seoul by Iwamiya Shōbei.
facts.quote: 주식회사 해시상회로 사명과 운영체계를 변경 (became Haesi Sanghoe Co.)

facts.text: A brass sinseollo it sold (National Folk Museum of Korea) has '京城海市商會製' written in ink on the lower part of its box, with a seal.
facts.quote: 묵서로 ‘京城海市商會製’가 적혀있고 직인 (inked 京城海市商會製, with a seal)

rows.meaning: Mitsukoshi department store, Keijō (Seoul) branch: retailer's seal or label on Korean souvenir crafts it sold.
rows.technique: seal on ceramics; paper label on lacquer; printed leaflet in sinseollo boxes (exact seal design not transcribed in the sources)
rows.date_note: Seoul sub-branch from 1906; full branch September 1929; new building and Korean Product Showroom 1930 (Oh). The end date is the end of colonial rule; the building later became Shinsegae (Oh).
rows.what_it_tells: Sold as a souvenir in colonial Seoul, most likely to a Japanese visitor; the celadon it sold came mainly from the Japanese-owned reproduction workshops Sanwa Kōraiyaki and Kanyō Kōraiyaki. Retailer's mark, not a maker's mark.
rows.cautions: The seal's exact characters and design are not transcribed in the sources read; '三越' is the store's name, not a confirmed reading of the seal. A Mitsukoshi seal marks a modern reproduction, not a Goryeo antique.

facts.text: The National Folk Museum of Korea holds a Goryeo-style celadon tea set with a Mitsukoshi seal, and the Shinsegae archive a mother-of-pearl lacquer dish set with a Mitsukoshi label.
facts.quote: celadon tea set with Mitsukoshi seal

facts.text: Mitsukoshi opened a Seoul sub-branch in 1906, became a full branch in September 1929 and opened its new building with a Korean Product Showroom in 1930; Kim calls it Korea's first department store (1929).
A sinseollo sold by Mitsukoshi's Seoul branch (1930s, National Folk Museum of Korea) came with a printed leaflet describing it as a Gyeonggi-made alloy speciality; it does not say Mitsukoshi made it.
facts.quote: 자신들이 판매하는 신선로에 대한 안내서 (a leaflet on the sinseollo it sold)

rows.meaning: Hwasin Sanghoe, a Seoul gold- and silversmithing firm founded in 1918 by the craftsman Shin Tae-hwa (신태화).
rows.technique: maker's inscription '화신명' (inscribed Hwasin) as described; form not transcribed
rows.date_note: Founded 1918; taken over by Park Heung-sik as Hwasin Sanghoe Co. in 1931, with Shin Tae-hwa still making the work (Kim, citing Jeong Ji-hee 2016).
rows.what_it_tells: High-quality Seoul silver of the colonial period; Princess Deokhye's 1931 wedding silver includes a Hwasin sinseollo (Kyushu National Museum).
rows.cautions: Single source chain (Kim 2021 citing Jeong Ji-hee's 2016 dissertation). The inscription's exact characters and form are not given; the hanja 和信 is the firm's name as written by Kim.

facts.text: Hwasin Sanghoe was a gold-and-silver works founded in 1918 by Shin Tae-hwa; Park Heung-sik took it over in 1931 as Hwasin Sanghoe Co., with Shin continuing to make the work.
facts.quote: 1918년 신태화가 설립한 금은세공회사 (gold-silver works founded by Shin Tae-hwa in 1918)

facts.text: A silver sinseollo with landscape design from Princess Deokhye's trousseau in the Kyushu National Museum was made by Hwasin Sanghoe, and is described as inscribed Hwasin (화신명).

rows.meaning: Sinhaeng Sanghoe, a large Seoul gold- and silversmithing works of the 1910s (craftsman Shin Tae-hwa, capital Kim Yeon-hak).
rows.technique: inscription '신행명' (inscribed Sinhaeng) as described; form not transcribed
rows.date_note: Active in the 1910s until Shin Tae-hwa founded Hwasin Sanghoe in 1918 (Kim). Start year approximate (1910s).
rows.what_it_tells: Colonial-period Seoul silver from one of the larger 1910s workshops.
rows.cautions: Single source; the inscription's exact form is not given.

facts.text: Sinhaeng Sanghoe was one of the larger gold-and-silver workshops in 1910s Seoul, set up with Shin Tae-hwa's skill and Kim Yeon-hak's capital, and lasted until Shin founded Hwasin Sanghoe in 1918; its advertisements list sinseollo.
facts.quote: 신태화의 기술과 김연학의 자본으로 설립 (founded on Shin Tae-hwa's skill and Kim Yeon-hak's capital)

facts.text: The Seoul Museum of History holds a sinseollo inscribed Sinhaeng with plum-blossom and ten-longevity designs (first half of the 20th century).

rows.meaning: 'Secret Garden ware': the name of the Goryeo-style celadon made by the Yi Royal Household Art Manufactory's ceramics department.
rows.technique: Attested as a product name (1919 press); whether wares carry 秘苑 or 秘苑磁器 as a mark is not confirmed in the sources read.
rows.date_note: Ceramics department added around 1910 (Encykorea); the name is reported in Maeil Sinbo, 3 April 1919 (cited by Oh).
rows.what_it_tells: Celadon from the royal workshop in Seoul, a colonial-period reproduction rather than a Goryeo antique.
rows.cautions: Product name only; the on-ware form of any mark is unconfirmed. Do not read a 秘苑 mark as proof without a documented example.

facts.text: While still the Yi Royal Household Art Workshop, its new ceramics department produced Goryeo-style celadon called 'Piwŏnjagi' (celadon made in Piwŏn).
The Seoul Museum of Craft Art's permanent display on colonial-period crafts lists 비원자기 among its keywords, with 이왕직미술품제작소 and 조선미술품제작소.

rows.meaning: Art name and studio name of Yu Geun-hyeong (1894-1993), the best-known 20th-century reviver of Goryeo celadon; his Icheon studio was the Haegang Goryeo Celadon Research Institute (1967).
wares: Goryeo-style inlaid celadon (maebyeong, tea bowls and others), including reproductions sold to tourists
rows.technique: Not documented in the sources read: no source describes the form of Haegang's signature or seal.
rows.date_note: First own kiln (Yeongdeungpo) 1926 per Nakamura; Haegang Goryeo Celadon Research Institute 1967; died 1993. The studio and museum continued under his family; production after 1993 not researched.
rows.what_it_tells: A genuine Haegang item is a modern (1920s-1990s) studio reproduction or reinterpretation of Goryeo celadon from the leading Korean reviver; from 1967 the studio made celadon copies commercially, largely for Japanese tourists.
rows.cautions: The name commands a premium (Nakamura saw items priced high 'just for being Haegang'), and the studio itself made reproductions, so the name alone proves genuine neither a Goryeo date nor Yu's own hand. Many potters trained at his kiln and set up their own studios in the 1970s, and his son Yu Gwang-yeol (柳光烈) also made and signed celadon. Encykorea says Yu worked from 1959 at the Sugwang-ri kiln it calls 광주요, while Kwangjuyo's founding is usually given as 1963 (see kwangjuyo row).

facts.text: Yu Geun-hyeong was born on 5 April 1894 in Seoul and died on 20 January 1993.
Haegang (海剛) was his art name.
facts.quote: 海剛とは柳氏の号 (Haegang is Mr Yu's art name)

facts.text: He learned the craft from 1911 at the Japanese-run Hanyang Goryeo-so.

Nakamura says he went to Japan in 1921 on Asakawa Noritaka's introduction to learn celadon in Kyoto, and opened his own Goryeo celadon kiln at Yeongdeungpo in 1926, when his and Hwang In-chun's were the only two celadon kilns in Korea.
facts.quote: 1926年に海剛は永登浦に高麗青磁の窯を開いた (in 1926 Haegang opened a celadon kiln at Yeongdeungpo)

facts.text: He won a gold medal at a Japanese exhibition in 1928.

From 1955 he worked at the Seongbuk-dong kiln (Kiln of Korean Art Society) and from autumn 1956 at the Daebang-dong kiln; when Daebang-dong closed in 1958 he moved to Sugwang-ri, Icheon, working from 1959 at the kiln Encykorea calls 광주요.
facts.quote: 이듬해부터 경기도 이천시 수광리의 광주요로 (from the next year, to Kwangjuyo at Sugwang-ri)

facts.text: He was recognized in 1963 as a celadon craftsman under the human cultural asset system and in 1988 as a Gyeonggi-do intangible heritage holder (청자장).
In 1967 he founded the Haegang Goryeo Celadon Research Institute and began full-scale production of celadon copies (maebyeong, tea bowls), selling successfully to Japanese tourists.
facts.quote: 청자 모조품을 본격적으로 생산 (began full-scale production of celadon copies)

facts.text: In 1990 he and his eldest son Yu Gwang-yeol founded the Haegang Ceramics Museum in Icheon.
In the 1970s potters from the Haegang kiln set up their own kilns: 金文植 (沙音窯), 金鐘浩 (松月窯), 金福漢 (漢青窯), 金世龍 (世昌陶芸), 李奇休 (扶林窯) and 李連休 (如泉窯).
facts.quote: 海剛窯からは … 独立した (from the Haegang kiln … set up on their own)

facts.text: Nakamura (2005) found Haegang items in Seoul shops priced high simply because they were Haegang works.
facts.quote: たんに海剛作品というだけで高額 (expensive just for being Haegang works)

rows.meaning: Yu Gwang-yeol, eldest son of Haegang Yu Geun-hyeong, celadon potter and director of the Haegang Ceramics Museum.
rows.technique: signature (form not documented in sources read)
rows.what_it_tells: Second-generation Haegang family work, not by Yu Geun-hyeong himself.
rows.cautions: Easily confused with his father's work. The English Wikipedia external link notes 'two extra dots' in his signature on a Smithsonian bowl; unverified (cross-check source only).

facts.text: Yu Gwang-yeol, Yu Geun-hyeong's eldest son, co-founded the Haegang Ceramics Museum with him in 1990.
facts.quote: 장남 유광열과 함께 해강도자미술관 (with eldest son Yu Gwang-yeol, the Haegang museum)

rows.meaning: Ji Sun-tak (1912-1993), art name Doam (陶庵), white-porcelain, buncheong and celadon potter; his Icheon workshop was Goryeo Doyo (高麗陶窯, 1966).
rows.technique: Not documented in the sources read (seller listings title him '도암 지순탁', but no source describes his seal).
rows.date_note: Goryeo Doyo founded about January 1966; Ji died September 1993.
rows.what_it_tells: Work from the largest Icheon reproduction workshop of the 1960s-70s, officially designated a maker of reproductions; most of its output was exported, so items are common in Western estates.
rows.cautions: Goryeo Doyo was officially a reproduction maker, so celadon or white porcelain from it can look like Goryeo or Joseon ware once the mark is ignored or absent. His name is also read 지순택 (Ji Sun-taek). His mark form is undocumented here; seller listings are leads only.

facts.text: Ji Sun-tak was born in Seoul on 30 April 1912 and died in September 1993; his art name was Doam (陶庵).
He and Haegang are the two first-generation revivers: Ji excelled at white porcelain, Yu at celadon.
facts.quote: 池が白磁を、柳が青磁を得意とした (Ji excelled at white porcelain, Yu at celadon)

facts.text: He worked at the Seongbuk-dong kiln (from 1956, with Yu Geun-hyeong) and was factory manager at the Daebang-dong kiln, which made export goods in traditional techniques.
facts.quote: 수출에 적합한 상품을 제작한 … 대방동가마 (the Daebang-dong kiln, making goods fit for export)

facts.text: About January 1966 he founded Goryeo Doyo (高麗陶窯, also called the Ji Sun-tak kiln) at Sugwang-ri, Icheon; it was designated by the Ministry of Culture and Information as a specialist maker of reproductions, was the largest workshop of its day, and exported most of its output.
facts.quote: 문화공보부로부터 모조품전문 제조업체로 선정 (designated a specialist reproduction maker)

facts.text: Goryeo Doyo, Haegang-yo and Kwangjuyo are described as the first-generation Icheon kilns from which many craftsmen came.
In 1988 he was recognized as a Gyeonggi-do intangible heritage holder for buncheong and white porcelain.
facts.quote: 분청 · 백자장 기예능보유자 (holder for buncheong and white porcelain)

facts.text: Potters who left his kiln to work on their own include 徐光洙 (韓陶窯), 朴富元 (陶元窯) and 金太漢.
facts.quote: 池順鐸窯からは、韓陶窯の徐光洙、陶元窯の朴富元

rows.meaning: Hancheong kiln of the potter Kim Bok-han (金福漢), a 1970s offshoot of the Haegang kiln.
rows.technique: Not documented in any source read: how (or whether) this maker marked its wares was not found.
rows.date_note: Set up in the 1970s (Nakamura); exact year not given.
rows.what_it_tells: A studio founded in the 1970s Icheon boom by a potter trained at a first-generation kiln; its wares date from the 1970s or later.
rows.cautions: Single source (Nakamura 2005, from interviews); characters as printed in a Japanese text (shinjitai forms such as 青 for 靑). Mark form unknown.

facts.text: Kim Bok-han (金福漢) left the Haegang kiln in the 1970s and set up the Hancheong kiln (漢青窯).
facts.quote: 漢青窯の金福漢 (Kim Bok-han of the Hancheong kiln)

facts.quote: 世昌陶芸の金世龍 (Kim Se-yong of Sechang Ceramics)

facts.text: Kim Mun-sik (金文植) left the Haegang kiln in the 1970s and set up the Saeum kiln (沙音窯).
facts.quote: 沙音窯の金文植 (Kim Mun-sik of the Saeum kiln)

facts.text: Kim Jong-ho (金鐘浩) left the Haegang kiln in the 1970s and set up the Songwol kiln (松月窯).
facts.quote: 松月窯の金鐘浩 (Kim Jong-ho of the Songwol kiln)

facts.quote: 扶林窯の李奇休 (Lee Gi-hyu of the Burim kiln)

facts.quote: 如泉窯の李連休 (Lee Yeon-hyu of the Yeocheon kiln)

facts.quote: 韓陶窯の徐光洙 (Seo Gwang-su of the Hando kiln)

facts.quote: 陶元窯の朴富元 (Park Bu-won of the Dowon kiln)

rows.technique: Not documented in any source read: how (or whether) this maker marked its wares was not found.
